gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Lowercase letters with the stature of cast iron capitals, all drawn in one constant stroke width, lead Edo SZ with real presence. Noto Sans Ethiopic adds a sturdy, tall-bodied counterweight.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Classic in spirit, Edo SZ stands its lowercase tall as cast iron capitals, every terminal ending as wide as it began. Noto Sans Georgian lets text run on comfortably, its open curves and short ascender stems never crowding.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-glagoliti: Edo SZ stands tall, every stroke drawn like a ballpoint line. It makes big, confident shapes, while Noto Sans Glagolitic is the one for clear, open round letters at small sizes.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Cultural weight comes from Edo SZ, its lowercase standing like cast iron capitals in a stroke that never varies. And Noto Sans Gothic, with its parenthesis-round counters, can stay modest in size without losing clarity.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Cast-iron stature, no thinning: Edo SZ keeps its bowls full at the sides. Noto Sans Grantha does the quieter work, with tall little letters that never snag on a closed-up bowl.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Noto Sans Gujarati lets its curved strokes stop short of turning inward, leaving large open counters. And Edo SZ takes the showpiece role, each glyph drawn with one-tip simplicity.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-g: Round letters whose walls match the straight ones in weight give Edo SZ a cast-iron stature in lowercase. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi then reads smoothly, cut-back terminals leaving gaps.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Noto Sans Gurmukhi has terminals that point outward like tongs. Edo SZ, cut from one gauge of tubing, deserves large sizes, while the sans-serif body is happy at modest ones.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Strokes that look traced with a marker give Edo SZ lowercase the stature of cast iron capitals. And it earns its keep big and short, leaving Noto Sans Hanunoo to fill lines with open, readable terminals.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Noto Sans Hebrew packs a dominant midsection into each line and leaves wide gaps between curve ends and stems. But shrink Edo SZ and its wire-like monoline skeleton fades from view.
